subject: dragonfly
reasoning:
I'm planning to build a dragonfly model with the SDK using realistic proportions—around 7cm body length—and deciding whether to show it perched on the ground or in flight.

For the skeleton, I'll set up a thorax root joint, an abdomen chain going backward, a head and jaw forward, four wing joints, and six leg joints with hip/knee/foot segments. Since I'm unsure of the exact API signatures for chains and roles, I'll try passing role options into the joint and chain calls and hope extra properties are tolerated at runtime even if the types aren't fully documented.

For body geometry, rather than relying on uncertain "dir/aim" parameters for part orientation, I'll pre-rotate each geometry myself so its axis points along Z, which is safer. I'm now constructing the thorax as a scaled sphere to form an ellipsoid body segment positioned near the top of the model.

Continuing the build out: the head attaches via a joint with compound eyes as colored spheres, plus a jawed mouth structure with upper and lower parts split between the head and a separate jaw joint. The abdomen becomes a chain of ten tapering segments with alternating color bands for a banded look, and the legs are three pairs hinged at the thorax, angling outward and down to reach the ground plane.

I decide to write a small helper function that builds a cylinder oriented between any two points by baking the transform directly into the geometry in model space, then attaching it to a bone with no extra offset needed. I plan to reuse this same baked-geometry approach for every part of the model, and now I'm sketching out four wings attached near the top of the thorax, extending sideways and swept back, using a flat shape geometry for the wing outlines.

Working through the wing geometry, I'm defining the wing's shape in span/chord coordinates and figuring out how rotating it into the XZ plane maps those coordinates, then mirroring the shape for the opposite side by flipping the X scale.

For mirroring I'll just reverse the point order when the sign is negative, since ExtrudeGeometry handles either winding direction automatically. For the wing material I'm going with a pale translucent blue-green color and adding thin dark vein details plus a small pterostigma box near the tip, baking these as simple thin boxes, then positioning and slightly tilting the wings for a resting pose.

Now I'm working out positioning details: separating forewing and hindwing y-values slightly to avoid z-fighting, setting ground contact points for legs, and planning small cerci appendages and dark pupil spheres for the eyes. I'm also designing a helper function that builds each limb segment as an oriented cylinder between two points using quaternion rotation and matrix composition, plus a joint-naming scheme for the legs with proper parent-child hierarchy.
